constraints: 4-digit addends, multiple carries
hints: Align columns and begin at ones.
Add each column with any incoming carry and exchange full tens leftward.
Continue through thousands and check by reversing with subtraction.

constraints: minuend contains zeros requiring a chain borrow
hints: When a column needs a borrow, find the next nonzero place to its left.
Exchange through every zero column, recording each changed digit.
Subtract with those changed digits and verify by addition.

constraints: two operations, numbers up to 4 digits
hints: Complete any grouped subtotal before ungrouped operations.
Then add or subtract left to right, preserving each sign and intermediate result.
Check that both operations and all quantities were used once.

constraints: one operation; numbers up to 4 digits
hints: What quantities and change or comparison words tell you what relationship to model?
Write one number sentence for each step, carrying the result of the first step into the next when needed.
Check that your final quantity answers the question asked and has the right direction or unit.

constraints: two operations; numbers up to 3 digits
hints: What quantities and change or comparison words tell you what relationship to model?
Write one number sentence for each step, carrying the result of the first step into the next when needed.
Check that your final quantity answers the question asked and has the right direction or unit.

constraints: difference/comparison language; up to 4 digits
hints: Identify the larger quantity, smaller quantity, and their difference.
Use the rule: the larger quantity equals the smaller quantity plus the difference; identify the unknown role and use addition or subtraction accordingly.
Check that the result belongs to the person or quantity the question asks about.

constraints: 1-2 digit number times 10, 100, or 1000
hints: Identify how many factors of ten multiply the basic number.
Move its digits left one place for each factor, filling empty whole-number places with zeros.
Check the number of added place values matches the power of ten.

constraints: both factors end in zeros; underlying fact from the tables
hints: What basic multiplication fact remains when the factors are viewed without their ending zeros?
Use that fact, then account for every factor of ten contributed by the original factors.
Check the size: multiplying by a power of ten should move the value to a larger place.

constraints: 2-digit x 1-digit
hints: Split the two-digit factor into tens and ones.
Multiply each part by the one-digit factor.
Add the two partial products and check their place values.

constraints: 3-digit x 1-digit, may include an internal zero
hints: Separate hundreds, tens, and ones, retaining a zero column when present.
Multiply every place-value contribution by the one-digit factor.
Add the contributions and estimate the size using rounded factors.

constraints: one factor near a round number
hints: Write one factor as a nearby round number plus or minus a small difference.
Multiply the round number and the small difference by the other factor.
Add or subtract that correction in the matching direction.

constraints: 2-digit x 2-digit
hints: Which place-value parts of each factor must be multiplied?
Make partial products for each place-value pair and align them with their values before adding.
Estimate with rounded factors, then compare the estimate with the combined partial products.

constraints: 3-digit x 2-digit
hints: Which place-value parts of each factor must be multiplied?
Make partial products for each place-value pair and align them with their values before adding.
Estimate with rounded factors, then compare the estimate with the combined partial products.

constraints: 2-digit x 2-digit; show or check with partial products
hints: Which place-value parts of each factor must be multiplied?
Make partial products for each place-value pair and align them with their values before adding.
Estimate with rounded factors, then compare the estimate with the combined partial products.

constraints: 2-digit dividend, 1-digit divisor, nonzero remainder; answer as 'q Rr'
hints: Find the greatest multiple of the divisor that does not exceed the dividend.
Its multiplier is the quotient; subtract that multiple to find what remains.
Check the remainder is smaller than the divisor and use the requested quotient-remainder form.

objective: Checking with divisor x quotient + remainder
constraints: remainder strictly smaller than the divisor
hints: Find the greatest multiple of the divisor that does not exceed the dividend.
Use its multiplier as quotient and subtract for the remainder.
Check divisor times quotient plus remainder equals dividend and the remainder is nonnegative and smaller.

constraints: context decides whether to drop or round up the remainder
hints: First complete the division into full groups and a remainder.
Decide whether the context counts only full groups or needs capacity for every item.
Use one additional group only when a leftover item still needs capacity.

constraints: 2-digit dividend, 1-digit divisor, divides evenly
hints: Begin with the leftmost available part of the dividend and decide how many divisor groups fit.
Multiply that quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, bring down the next digit, and repeat.
Check the quotient and any remainder with divisor times quotient plus remainder.

constraints: 3-digit dividend, 1-digit divisor, divides evenly
hints: Begin with the leftmost available part of the dividend and decide how many divisor groups fit.
Multiply that quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, bring down the next digit, and repeat.
Check the quotient and any remainder with divisor times quotient plus remainder.

constraints: 3-digit dividend, 1-digit divisor, nonzero remainder; answer as 'q Rr'
hints: Begin with the leftmost available part of the dividend and decide how many divisor groups fit.
Multiply that quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, bring down the next digit, and repeat.
Check the quotient and any remainder with divisor times quotient plus remainder.

constraints: 4-digit dividend, 1-digit divisor
hints: Begin with the leftmost available part of the dividend and decide how many divisor groups fit.
Multiply that quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, bring down the next digit, and repeat.
Check the quotient and any remainder with divisor times quotient plus remainder.

constraints: 3-digit dividend, 2-digit divisor, divides evenly
hints: Estimate a quotient digit using nearby multiples of the divisor.
Multiply by the original divisor and adjust until it fits but the next multiple does not.
Subtract, bring down, and repeat for the next place.

constraints: 2-digit divisor, nonzero remainder; answer as 'q Rr'
hints: Estimate and verify each quotient digit with the actual two-digit divisor.
Adjust until the actual divisor multiple fits the current partial dividend but the next multiple does not; then subtract and continue.
Check the final remainder is smaller than the divisor and report both components.
